_comment: The tempo lab: composition measured against a clock, with no content in the way.
`scons matrix` hands the whole budget over at once, so it cannot see anything whose value depends on arriving
early -- price above all. The campaign sweep can, but it is denominated in shipped levels, and a level is
narrative: it has pacing, escalation, and some are written to be lost. A win rate over one of those measures
the story, not the roster.
So these four engagements carry no story. They are a controlled comparison: identical base, and the *same
twenty hostiles* -- grime 8, wrecker 5, hound 3, jackal 2, mason 2. The only variable is when that force
arrives. Anything that separates the four is a tempo effect and nothing else.
The purse differs per engagement (rush 100, spike 120, grind 40, escalation 40) and is not a free parameter:
the same force delivered faster is simply harder, so one purse cannot put four schedules in the band where
compositions come apart. Each was swept and set where they do. This is a hand-calibrated stand-in for the
right measurement, which is the *critical purse* -- bisect starting energy per (composition, engagement) the
way `scons matrix` bisects budget. Win rate at a fixed purse is a step function: most cells read 0% or 100%,
so this table ranks compositions but does not measure the distance between them.
tempo_rush        all twenty inside 30s, fast units first  -- punishes an opening spent banking
tempo_spike       a minute of nothing, then all twenty     -- rewards the bank the rush punishes
tempo_grind       one every six seconds for two minutes    -- no spike to answer, the economy is the limit
tempo_escalation  cheap first, heavy last, same two minutes -- the right answer changes mid-match
Rows are compositions rather than spending heuristics, because composition is the question. `greedy` and
`defensive` are kept as reference lines: they vary when to spend, never what to buy.
Read it per (level, policy) and paired by seed. A policy total across four engagements that disagree with each
other is the one number here that carries no information.
_owned_upgrades_note: The three unit_unlock cards, and nothing else. Without them the roster is base_units -- breacher alone -- and every composition policy silently collapses to the same force.
